facts.fact: AIP states that the Citiweb software deployed by ONECI allows births, marriages, deaths and other acts of civil life to be captured at the civil status centres.

AIP states that all the civil status centres of the town halls and sub-prefectures were supplied at the end of 2025 with computer equipment carrying the Citiweb software; this is a statement of centres equipped, with no numerator or denominator, and a trainer says the training is what will allow the software's effective application.
AIP states that ONECI, whose mission is to modernise civil status, deployed Citiweb in the town halls and sub-prefectures and trains its own civil status agents on it.

At the end of 2025 all town hall and sub-prefecture civil status centres were supplied with computers carrying Citiweb, and training of agents began then, with agents of several regions already trained, per AIP.

From 27 to 29 July 2026 ONECI trained 44 civil status agents of the Gôh region's town halls and sub-prefectures at Gagnoa on the new Citiweb software, deployed there with a view to launching the modernisation of civil status; an ONECI trainer said agents in several centres were following procedures of their own devising.

systems.tiers: civil status centres of town halls (mairies) and sub-prefectures, all equipped at the end of 2025
